samples: This module gives you a generic last-in first-out stack (push, pop, peek, and a size/emptiness check) that is immutable, so each operation returns a new stack rather than changing the old one, and popping or peeking an empty stack yields nothing instead of an error. It also offers a pure `balanced` function that checks whether round and square brackets in a piece of text are properly closed in the correct order, ignoring all other characters. It needs no special permissions, and it ships with examples and tests, but it only handles `()` and `[]` (not curly braces) and copies the list on each push or pop, so it suits small inputs better than performance-critical ones.

This module gives you a generic, immutable last-in first-out stack (push, pop, peek, and a size/emptiness check), where each operation returns a new stack and popping or peeking an empty one yields nothing rather than an error. It also provides a `balanced` function that checks whether every round and square bracket in a piece of text is closed by its matching partner in the correct order, ignoring all other characters. It is pure (no effects) and includes examples and tests, so it is a safe, self-contained choice if you need either a basic stack or simple bracket validation, though it only handles `()` and `[]`, not curly braces.

It is pure (no effects needed) and includes examples and tests, so it is a safe, self-contained choice if you need a simple stack or a quick round/square bracket validator, though it does not handle curly braces.
